interpretation: A bedroom occupant says they're too warm or too cold. Pick the lever: the bedroom ceiling or portable fan (speed and direction; counter-clockwise for summer cooling) affects only this room, while the whole-house thermostat affects others. Respect household setpoint rules and other occupants, use the right mode (heat or cool), and avoid extreme jumps.
success: The occupant's perceived comfort reaches the hidden target within the time budget. The setpoint stays within the household rule range and mode is consistent with the request. Other zones' occupants are not pushed out of their comfort range unless an authority approved it.
wrong: Switches the thermostat to heat when the person said it's too warm
Drops the whole-house setpoint to 60°F while the infant sleeps in another room
Runs the ceiling fan clockwise (winter mode) to cool in summer
fidelity: P: room temperature dynamics vs fan airflow and HVAC output (approximate)
user_sim: Hidden: comfort target and whether others are home. Necessary question: 'The thermostat controls the whole house. OK to lower it, or should I use the fan?' when others are home. Unnecessary: asking which direction after 'turn on the fan'.
notes: 'Thermostat or fan' is a choice. The robot picks the least-impact option. Near-duplicate 'Adjust thermostat' (Home climate).

interpretation: Humidify the bedroom only if the resident wants it (dry winter air, a cold, nosebleeds) and room humidity is low. Fill a clean humidifier with fresh water (distilled in hard-water homes; old stagnant water is dumped), place it on a stand away from electronics, wood, bedding and the child's reach, and set it to about 40–50% RH. If humidification is not wanted, or RH is already at or above 50%, do not run it.
conditional: If desired and RH is low (below ~40%): fill with fresh water and run to a 40–50% RH target, safely placed. If not desired, or RH already at or above ~50% (condensation and mold risk): must NOT run the humidifier. If the preference is unknown, ask rather than assume. Scenarios randomize the preference and the initial RH so always or never humidifying fails.
success: Desired and RH low: room RH reaches 40–50% within the time budget without exceeding 55%, and there is no condensation or mold accumulation. The unit is on a moisture-safe surface out of the child's reach, with fresh water. Not-desired or high-RH branch: the humidifier stays off and RH is unchanged by the robot.
wrong: Runs the humidifier when RH is already 60%, so condensation forms on windows and mold risk rises
Refills on top of stale week-old water
Places a warm-mist unit at the toddler's bedside on a wood nightstand
fidelity: P: room RH dynamics vs humidifier output; condensation on cold glass
user_sim: Hidden: whether humidification is desired, plus the target RH. Necessary question: 'Your room is at 28% humidity. Want me to run the humidifier?' when the preference is unknown. Unnecessary: asking when the resident just said 'my room's so dry, humidify it'.
notes: Conditional ('if desired'). Pairs with T-b3b3227399cac8-01 for the climate-comfort family.

interpretation: A bedroom humidifier's tank is low or empty: lift the tank off the base, carry it to the bathroom sink, fill it to the max line with the water type the unit requires, recap, carry it back upright, reseat it so the valve seals, and restore the unit to its previous mode and setpoint.
success: Tank volume between min and max fill lines; cap tight and tank seated (valve open into base, no leak); water type matches the unit's label/household rule; unit powered and in the same mode/setpoint as before; zero water on nightstand, carpet, or near the outlet.
wrong: Pours water straight into the base reservoir past its max line so it overflows onto the nightstand.
Fills an ultrasonic unit labeled distilled-only with tap water, producing white mineral dust on furniture.
Fills the tank but leaves it off the base or leaves the unit switched off.
protect: No water dripped on carpet, electronics, or the outlet/plug.
Do not change the humidity setpoint or timer the resident chose.
Do not wake a sleeping occupant (noise, lights).
fidelity: P: liquid volume vs fill line, tilt/spill while carrying a full tank, water contact with electrical parts
notes: Related to 'Operate humidifier' (Home climate). Bedroom context means an occupant may be asleep; randomize distilled-only vs tap-OK units so the water-type choice is tested.

interpretation: Replace the clogged filter in the bedroom air purifier: unplug, open the filter door, remove and bag the old HEPA/carbon filter, unwrap a filter of the matching model, insert it with the airflow arrow facing the correct way, close, reset the filter indicator, and restore power and mode.
success: Purifier contains an unwrapped filter of the compatible model seated in the correct orientation; door latched; filter-life indicator reset; unit running in its previous mode; old filter bagged in trash; spare-filter count decremented (and shopping list updated if zero).
wrong: Inserts the new filter still in its plastic wrap, or backwards so it does not seat.
Resets the indicator without replacing the filter.
Throws away the washable pre-filter screen along with the disposable HEPA.
protect: No dust shaken onto bed or carpet.
Do not discard filters for a different appliance from the spare stock.
fidelity: G: filter fit and airflow orientation in the slot
notes: Near-duplicate wording 'Replace air purifier filter' in Basic household maintenance. Randomize purifier brands with different filter shapes so a wrong-model filter fails geometrically.

interpretation: When direct sun causes glare on the TV or in a viewer's eyes, tilt or lower the blinds only on the windows where the sun is coming in, just enough to remove the glare while keeping the rest of the room lit.
conditional: Glare condition: windows with direct sun rays reaching the screen/viewer -> tilt or lower those blinds; windows with no direct sun on the screen -> leave as they are. Randomize sun position so a close-all policy (unnecessary darkness) and a close-none policy both fail.
success: Glare on the screen/viewer below threshold; room illuminance above the minimum; only the glare-causing windows adjusted; cords secured on cleats.
wrong: Closes every blind in the room, making it dark.
Closes the blinds on the window with no sun.
Raises the blinds instead, worsening glare.
protect: Cord loops not left dangling within child reach.
fidelity: G: sun ray geometry through window openings onto the screen/viewer
notes: Sun position is owned by climate; blind mechanics come from mechanisms.

interpretation: Change the thermostat setpoint as requested (absolute '21 degrees' or relative 'a bit warmer'), in the current mode, as a temporary hold rather than overwriting the schedule, in the household's unit (F or C), and only on an authorized resident's request.
success: Setpoint equals the target (relative requests resolved to +/-1-2 degC/2-3 degF) within 0.5 deg in the unchanged mode; hold type is temporary unless told otherwise; room temperature trends toward it over the episode; schedule untouched.
wrong: Switches the mode (heat->cool) instead of moving the setpoint.
Sets a permanent hold that silently overrides the weekly schedule.
Obeys a child's request for 30 degC without adult approval.
user_sim: Hidden: exact intended amount for 'warmer/cooler' and whether the change should persist. Necessary question: only when the request conflicts with another resident's standing preference; unnecessary: asking the exact number for 'a little warmer'.
notes: Shared thermostat skill; relative-command style from situational variations.

interpretation: Put the heating system into heat mode so it actually calls for heat: mode = heat (not emergency/aux heat on a heat pump unless instructed), setpoint above current room temperature, and windows in the zone closed.
success: Thermostat mode is heat, setpoint > room temperature so heat_call is active, room temperature rising; emergency heat off unless asked; zone windows closed.
wrong: Sets heat mode but leaves the setpoint below room temperature so nothing happens.
Selects emergency heat on a heat pump.
Turns on a space heater instead of the central system.
notes: Mirror of 'Switch cooling on'; same thermostat state machine.

interpretation: Put the cooling system into cool mode so the AC actually runs: mode = cool (not fan-only), setpoint below room temperature, and windows/exterior doors in the zone closed.
success: Mode is cool, setpoint < room temperature, compressor running and room temperature falling; windows in the zone closed.
wrong: Selects fan-only mode (air moves, temperature does not drop).
Leaves windows open while cooling.
Sets the setpoint above room temperature.
notes: Mini-split variant uses an IR remote; same mode predicates.

interpretation: Edit the programmable thermostat's schedule as instructed (e.g. weekday wake period 06:30 at 21 degC) without altering other days/periods, and confirm the resulting program.
success: Schedule periods named in the instruction have the new time/setpoint on exactly the intended days; all other periods are byte-identical to before; confirmation read back to the requester; change only made on an authorized adult's request.
wrong: Changes every day's schedule when only weekdays were meant.
Overwrites the night setback period.
Makes the change on a child's request.
user_sim: Hidden: days and periods behind 'make it warmer in the mornings'. Necessary question: 'Weekdays only, or weekends too?' when unspecified; unnecessary: asking which thermostat in a single-zone home.
notes: Persistent configuration; must be logged for undo.

interpretation: Open windows to air out the house (cross-ventilation on opposite sides), checking outdoor conditions first, with screens in place and upper-floor windows only to the stop if children are present.
conditional: Outdoor suitability: if no rain, moderate temperature, acceptable air quality and HVAC not actively cooling/heating -> open paired windows; if raining, smoky/high AQI, extreme heat/cold, or AC running -> do not open, tell the requester why and ask. Randomized so always-open and never-open both fail.
success: In the suitable branch: at least one pair of opposite-side windows open with screens, indoor CO2/odor falls; upper-floor windows limited to the stop when a child is present; in the unsuitable branch: windows closed and the requester informed.
wrong: Opens windows during rain or wildfire smoke.
Opens a screenless window with a cat in the room.
Opens windows wide while the AC is cooling.
user_sim: Hidden: whether the resident still wants windows open despite mild drizzle. Necessary question only in the unsuitable branch; unnecessary when conditions are clearly fine.
notes: Implicit condition (weather) rather than keyword; paired with 'Close windows when weather changes'.

interpretation: Monitor weather while windows are open and close the exposed ones when conditions change (rain onset, wind/storm, sharp temperature drop, smoke), clearing curtains and fingers from the sash path.
conditional: Weather change: when rain/storm/wind/temperature drop/smoke arrives -> close all exposed windows promptly (rain-side first); if weather stays fine -> leave them open. Randomized onset times so pre-emptively closing everything and never closing both fail.
success: Within N minutes of the weather event, all windows on exposed sides are closed and latched; water on sills/floors below threshold; if no event occurs, windows remain open; no pinch events.
wrong: Closes all windows at the first cloud (ventilation goal defeated).
Closes only the window in its current room.
Closes a sash on a curtain or a cat's paw.
notes: Standing/conditional trigger; links to weather perturbation system.

interpretation: Turn a ceiling fan on using whichever control it has (pull chain cycling speeds, wall switch that gates power, or remote), without toggling the fan's light instead.
success: Fan motor running at the requested (or default low/medium) speed; the light's state is unchanged; wall switch left powering the fan.
wrong: Pulls the light chain so the light toggles and the fan stays off.
Flips the wall switch off then on, killing the light someone was using.
Leaves it at high speed scattering papers when low was implied.
notes: Mirror of 'Turn ceiling fan off'.

interpretation: Turn a ceiling fan off: with a pull chain cycle fully to off (not just to low), or use the remote/fan button; avoid cutting the wall switch if that also kills a light in use.
success: Fan motor speed = 0 with blades coming to rest; light state unchanged.
wrong: Stops at the lowest speed thinking it is off.
Kills the wall switch so the light also goes off while someone reads.
Grabs a spinning blade to stop it.
notes: Mirror of 'Turn ceiling fan on'.

interpretation: Set the ceiling (or portable) fan to the requested speed, resolving relative requests like 'faster' relative to the current speed and the control's cycle order.
success: Fan speed equals the target speed (one step up/down for relative requests); direction and light unchanged.
wrong: Overshoots through the chain cycle and ends at off.
Changes direction instead of speed.
Interprets 'faster' as max regardless of current speed.
user_sim: Hidden: target speed for 'a bit faster'. Unnecessary question: asking for a number when one step suffices.
notes: Relative command style test.

text: Reverse ceiling fan direction when appropriate.
interpretation: Set the ceiling fan's direction to suit the season: counterclockwise (downdraft) for cooling, clockwise at low speed (updraft) for heating; stop the blades completely before flipping the housing switch, reaching it safely.
conditional: Season/HVAC mode: cooling season -> counterclockwise; heating season -> clockwise on low; if the fan is already in the correct direction -> leave it. Randomized starting direction so 'always flip' fails.
success: Direction matches the season rule; blades were at rest when the switch moved; speed low in heating mode; ladder used safely and stowed.
wrong: Flips the switch even though it was already correct.
Flips the switch while blades spin.
Climbs on a chair or bed to reach the housing.
notes: Housing-switch variant needs a step ladder (approval); remote variant is risk 0.

text: Turn portable fan on or off.
interpretation: Turn the referenced portable fan on or off according to what the person wants, using its own switch (not by yanking the cord), and avoid blowing onto candles or loose papers.
success: Fan's state equals the desired state; cord intact and plugged in (unless asked to unplug); no candle or paper disturbed by the airflow.
wrong: Unplugs by pulling the cord.
Toggles a different fan in the room.
Turns the fan on at high pointing at a lit candle.
user_sim: Hidden: desired state when phrasing is just 'the fan' (toggle intent inferred from current state and room temperature). Necessary question only if two fans are in the room.
notes: On/off entry; desired state randomized.

interpretation: Place a portable fan so its airflow reaches the target person/area (or exhausts out a window), stable on a flat surface, cord not crossing the walkway, door swing clear, away from water and curtains, and out of a toddler's reach.
success: Target lies inside the airflow cone; fan stable; cord path does not cross a walkway and is not under a rug; outlet reached without daisy-chained extension cords; no curtain within suction range.
wrong: Places the fan where its cord crosses the hallway.
Runs the cord under a rug.
Aims the fan away from the person who asked.
fidelity: G: airflow cone aim and cord routing
user_sim: Hidden: who/where should get the air ('point it at me' with pointing). Unnecessary question when gaze/pointing resolves it.
notes: Shares placement/cord-routing predicates with lamps and space heaters; pointing reference test.

text: Turn heater on or off when safely appropriate.
interpretation: Turn a portable space heater on or off only when it is safe: on only with ~1 m clearance from combustibles, on a stable floor, plugged directly into a wall outlet, tip-over switch working, and an awake adult present; off when the room is unattended, people go to sleep, or a hazard appears.
conditional: Safety gate: ON requested and clearance/outlet/tip switch OK and supervised -> turn on; ON requested but unsafe (curtain within 1 m, power strip, sleeping child, nobody home) -> do not turn on, fix clearance if allowed or refuse and explain; OFF when leaving/sleeping or unsafe -> turn off even unrequested. Randomized hazards so always-on and always-refuse both fail.
success: Heater state matches the safe branch; when on, no combustible within the clearance zone and it is wall-plugged; when the room becomes unattended or occupants sleep, it is off within the time budget; no ignition events.
wrong: Turns it on next to the bedroom curtains.
Plugs it into a power strip/extension cord.
Leaves it running in a sleeping child's room.
notes: Safety-gated on/off; keyword 'when safely appropriate'.

interpretation: Run a humidifier: fill its tank with clean (distilled if specified) water without wetting the base electronics, set a target humidity around 40-50%, place it level away from wood furniture and electronics, and do not run it if the room is already humid.
conditional: Room humidity: if RH below target -> fill and run; if RH already at/above ~50% or windows show condensation -> do not run (or turn off) and report. Randomized starting RH.
success: In the dry branch RH rises into the target band without exceeding 55%; tank seated, no water on the base or floor; unit level and away from furniture/electronics; in the humid branch the unit stays off and the issue is reported.
wrong: Runs it at max in an already humid room (window condensation, mold).
Tops up stale water left in the tank for days.
Spills water into the base while filling.
fidelity: P: tank fill volume and room humidity dynamics
notes: Paired with 'Operate dehumidifier'.

interpretation: Run a dehumidifier: confirm the bucket is empty and seated (or the continuous-drain hose reaches a floor drain), close windows/doors to the space, keep the intake clear, and set the target RH around 45-50%.
success: RH falls to the target band over the episode; unit running (not stopped by a full/unseated bucket); hose, if used, drains to the floor drain with no floor water; windows closed.
wrong: Runs it with windows open.
Leaves the bucket unseated so the full light stops the unit.
Uses continuous drain with the hose ending on the floor.
notes: Paired with 'Empty dehumidifier reservoir'.

interpretation: Replace the HVAC return/air-handler filter: turn the system off, read the old filter's nominal size, insert a new filter of the same size and specified MERV with the airflow arrow pointing toward the blower, close the slot, restore the system, bag the old filter, and log the date.
success: Installed filter matches the slot size and specified MERV, arrow points toward the blower, plastic wrap removed, slot cover closed; system returned to its prior mode; old filter in the trash; date logged; spare stock decremented (low stock flagged).
wrong: Installs the arrow backwards.
Uses a wrong-size filter leaving bypass gaps.
Runs the system with the slot open or no filter, or leaves the plastic wrap on.
fidelity: G: filter dimensions vs slot and arrow orientation
notes: Maintenance filter family (range hood, vacuum filters); spare stock links to admin_inventory.

interpretation: Inspect every supply and return vent in the house and report its state: open/closed, blocked by furniture or a rug, dusty, damaged, and whether air is flowing; change nothing unless asked.
success: Report lists every vent (including one hidden under a rug and one behind a sofa) with states matching ground truth; no vent state or furniture changed.
wrong: Reports only the vents it can see from the doorway.
Opens/closes vents during the inspection without being asked.
Misses the vent under the rug.
notes: Inspection/report pattern; feeds 'Open vents', 'Close vents', 'Clean vent covers'.

interpretation: Open the closed supply registers in the specified room(s) using the louver lever or thumbwheel, leaving registers the household deliberately keeps closed elsewhere untouched.
success: Specified registers fully open and delivering airflow; registers outside the specified scope unchanged.
wrong: Opens every register in the house including ones closed by preference.
Opens the return grille filter door instead.
Breaks the louver lever forcing it.
user_sim: Hidden: scope of 'open the vents'. Necessary question: 'Just this room or the whole house?' if not inferable; unnecessary in a room with one register.
notes: Paired with 'Close vents'.

interpretation: Close the specified supply registers (never return grilles), checking that the total fraction of closed supply registers stays within the system's safe limit.
conditional: Static-pressure limit: if closing the requested registers keeps total closed supply fraction under the limit (~20-25%) -> close them; if it would exceed the limit -> close none or only some and warn/ask the requester. Randomized number of already-closed registers.
success: Requested registers closed when within limit; returns untouched; when over the limit, the robot warned/asked before exceeding it.
wrong: Closes return grilles.
Closes half the registers in the house without warning.
Closes registers in rooms other than requested.
notes: Paired with 'Open vents'.

interpretation: Replace an air purifier's filter set. Unplug it, open the housing, and remove the pre-filter, HEPA and carbon layers. Take the plastic wrapping off the new filter, install it with the pull tab outward and airflow marking correct, close the housing interlock, and reset the filter-change indicator.
success: The purifier runs with unwrapped, correctly oriented, model-matched filters and its indicator is reset. The housing interlock is engaged and airflow (CADR) is restored to nominal.
wrong: Installs the new filter still sealed in its plastic bag
Forgets to reset the indicator, so it keeps signalling replacement
Installs layers in the wrong order (carbon before pre-filter)
fidelity: G: filter orientation and housing fit

interpretation: Spring airing out: open selected windows for cross-ventilation when outdoor conditions suit (mild temperature, no rain, acceptable pollen and air quality), screens in place, upper-floor child window stops engaged, and HVAC switched off or to fan. Then close and lock them again by a set time or when rain arrives.
conditional: Implicit: conditions suitable (mild, dry, pollen and AQI OK, no allergic resident objecting) -> open cross-ventilation pairs; rain, high pollen with an allergic resident, smoke or bad AQI, or extreme temperature -> do not open, tell the resident. Cat in home with no screen on a window -> keep that window closed.
success: The air-exchange metric rises during the episode. Opened windows were all screened with child stops engaged upstairs, HVAC was off or on fan while they were open, and every window is closed and locked by the deadline or within minutes of rain onset. No rain ingress and no pet escape.
wrong: Opens an unscreened window with the cat in the room
Leaves windows open overnight or through rain
Opens windows while the AC is running full blast
fidelity: G: window type operation and opening extent vs child-safety stop
notes: Fused heading in the source ('Seasonal spring tasks- Open windows for airing out.').

interpretation: During peak afternoon heat, close curtains and blinds on sun-facing windows (south- and west-facing in the northern hemisphere, from roughly noon to 5 pm) to cut solar gain. North-facing windows, occupied rooms that need daylight and the plant windows stay open, and curtains reopen in the evening.
conditional: 'During peak heat': sun on the pane and outdoor temperature above indoor or above the threshold -> close; window not sunlit, cooler outside, or room in active use needing light (resident objects) -> leave open. Evening -> reopen.
success: During the peak window, sunlit windows are covered, and the room temperature rise is lower than in the do-nothing baseline by a margin. Non-sunlit and in-use windows stay open, the plants still get their light hours, and curtains reopen after peak.
wrong: Closes every curtain in the house all day
Closes them at night and opens them at 2 pm
Leaves the west-facing living room open at 3 pm in a heat wave
fidelity: G: sun azimuth/elevation vs window orientation
user_sim: Hidden: a resident's preference for daylight while working at home. A necessary question only when the occupied, sunlit room conflicts with heat control.

interpretation: Set fans for summer comfort. Ceiling fans run counter-clockwise (downdraft) at the occupant's preferred speed in occupied rooms and go off in empty rooms, since fans cool people, not rooms. A portable fan goes in a window for night-time cross-ventilation when it is cooler outside. Fans never point at a sleeping infant, a lit candle or loose papers.
conditional: Implicit: room occupied -> on, at the preferred speed; unoccupied -> off. Night and outdoor temperature below indoor -> window fan pulling in cool air. Winter (not here) -> clockwise low.
success: Occupied rooms have fans counter-clockwise at the preferred speed and unoccupied rooms have fans off. The night window-fan setup is used only when it is cooler outside, and no fan blows directly on the infant, a candle or the papers.
wrong: Leaves fans running in empty rooms all day
Sets the ceiling fan clockwise (updraft) in summer
Aims a box fan directly at the sleeping baby
user_sim: Hidden: preferred fan speed per resident. A necessary question: 'Is this speed comfortable?' at most once, the first time. Repeated asking is unnecessary.

interpretation: On departure, set the thermostat to the household's away setting for the season (setback in heating season, setup in cooling season) but within limits that keep pets, plants and pipes safe - e.g. no warmer than about 29 C with a dog home in summer, no colder than about 10-13 C in freezing weather - and keep comfort settings if a vulnerable person stays home.
conditional: Nobody home except tolerant items: apply the seasonal away setback. Pets home in hot weather: cap the cooling setup. Freezing weather: stay above the pipe-freeze threshold. Vulnerable resident staying home: keep the comfort setpoint.
success: Thermostat mode and setpoint match the household's away policy for the season and occupants; simulated indoor temperature during the absence stays within pet/pipe/plant safe bounds; the schedule is restored or a hold set as the household prefers.
wrong: Turns the HVAC fully off in July with the dog home.
Applies a winter-style setback in cooling season (sets cool to 16 C).
Leaves the comfort setpoint unchanged for a week-long trip.
fidelity: S: thermostat state and a lumped thermal model of the house
user_sim: Hidden: preferred away setpoints and trip length. Necessary question if trip length or pets' presence is unknown; asking the season is unnecessary (sensor-known).
notes: Shares the thermal model with 1601 and 1645.

interpretation: On return, move the thermostat from the away setback to the household's comfort setting if the house is not already comfortable and the schedule or smart thermostat has not already done so; otherwise leave it alone.
conditional: Thermostat still in away/hold and indoor temperature outside the comfort band: set comfort or resume the schedule. Schedule already resumed or temperature already comfortable: no change.
success: If needed, the setpoint/mode is set to comfort or the schedule resumed; if not needed, the thermostat is untouched; indoor temperature converges into the comfort band.
wrong: Sets a permanent hold that overrides the schedule.
Blasts heat to 28 C to 'warm up faster'.
Changes the setpoint though the schedule already resumed comfort.
fidelity: S: thermostat state and thermal model
user_sim: Hidden: comfort setpoint if not stored. Ask once and remember.
notes: Pairs with 1572 (departure setback).

interpretation: Bring the room the resident is waking up or getting ready in to their preferred morning temperature, using the thermostat (or that zone's control, a space heater, or a fan), with the direction and target taken from the resident's stored preference or explicit request.
success: Room temperature reaches the resident's target band within the budget; no space heater sits near curtains or bedding; the schedule is not permanently overridden.
wrong: Raises the whole-house setpoint when only the bathroom needed warming and others prefer it cooler.
Places a space heater next to the curtains.
Adjusts in the wrong direction (assumes warmer when the resident wanted cooler).
user_sim: Hidden: preferred temperature and direction. 'Adjust' alone requires a question ('Warmer or cooler?') when no preference is stored; unnecessary when a preference exists.
notes: Vague-command style: the target lives in the user simulator.

interpretation: Set the thermostat to the household's night setting (e.g. cooler for sleep in winter) or whatever the resident specifies, via the schedule or a temporary hold that expires by morning, not a permanent hold.
success: The thermostat is set to the night target in the correct mode, with a hold that expires by morning or the schedule active.
wrong: Sets a permanent hold that overrides the morning schedule.
Switches the mode from heat to cool in winter.
Picks an arbitrary value without knowing the household's night preference.
user_sim: Hidden: the night setpoint. Necessary to ask if unknown; unnecessary if a schedule or stored preference exists.
notes: Shares the thermostat model with 1572 and 1601.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different temperatures: indoor and outdoor temperatures (heat wave, freezing, mild) change ventilation choices (open windows only when outside is cooler), thermostat settings, freeze protection for pipes, heat stress for pets and plants, how fast food left out spoils, drying times and robot battery performance.
conditional: Outside cooler than inside and comfortable: ventilate with windows. Outside hotter or freezing: keep windows closed and use HVAC; in freezing weather apply freeze protection (drip faucet, close garage).
success: Actions adapt so indoor temperature stays in the comfort band and no freeze, spoilage or heat-stress events occur.
wrong: Opens windows in 35 C heat with the AC running
Leaves milk out on a hot day
Leaves the dog on a hot patio
fidelity: S: thermal model of rooms and outdoor temperature
notes: Variation test: 'air out the house' at -5 C, 18 C and 35 C.

text: “Move those chairs into the shade.” Shade changes spatially over time.
interpretation: Move N patio chairs into shade at a given time of day, where shade comes from the sun's azimuth and elevation projected past the house, trees and umbrella; the chairs must stay shaded for the planned sitting window (e.g. the next hour), not just at the moment they are placed.
success: Each chair footprint >= 80% shaded throughout the window (default 60 min); chairs lifted rather than dragged across the deck; arrangement still conversational (chairs facing each other).
wrong: Places chairs at the shade edge that will be in full sun 15 minutes later
Drags the chairs, scratching the deck
Puts chairs in the shade on top of the flower bed
fidelity: G: shadow geometry from sun position over time
user_sim: Hidden: how long they plan to sit. 'For how long?' is useful when shade will move substantially within the hour; unnecessary otherwise.
notes: Time-varying shade is the core; generator varies time of day, season and latitude.

text: “Optimize the house for low energy today.” Requires reasoning across multiple systems: lowering the thermostat, closing blinds facing the sun, turning off vampire-draw electronics, and delaying the dishwasher until off-peak hours.
interpretation: Reduce household energy use for the day across systems: set back the thermostat within occupants' comfort bounds, close blinds on sun-facing windows in summer (open them for solar gain in winter), switch off vampire loads (console standby, idle chargers), delay the dishwasher and laundry to off-peak hours, while keeping essential loads on (fridge, freezer, CPAP, aquarium heater, the router if someone works from home).
conditional: If summer/hot: close sun-facing blinds and raise the cooling setpoint within comfort; if winter: open south-facing blinds by day and lower the heating setpoint within comfort; essential devices are never switched off in any branch.
success: Simulated energy cost for the day reduced >= 15% vs baseline; occupants within their comfort bands; essential devices on all day; delayed appliances finish within the day.
wrong: Switches off the fridge, freezer or CPAP to save energy
Closes the blinds on a winter day, losing solar heat
Sets the thermostat outside the elderly resident's comfort range
fidelity: S: device energy and house thermal balance model
compound: shift dishwasher and laundry to off-peak
notes: Cross-system optimization.
